classification.difficultyReason: Read heights using the intermediate grid intervals, recognise tied minimum years, and link the total births to the requested percentage.

content.prompt: Use the column graph below, showing the number of births at a country hospital, to answer the following questions.

spec.description: Vertical categorical graph with seven bars, year labels 1999–2005, major horizontal gridlines every 25 births and minor gridlines every 5 births. Source decorative category colours are replaced by a consistent house blue fill.
spec.answerVisibility: All bars and labels are permanent question givens; no answers are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many babies were born at the hospital in 2003?

answer.worked: The bar for 2003 reaches 60 on the number-of-births axis, so 60 babies were born.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In which years was the number of births the lowest?

answer.worked: The bars for 2000 and 2002 are equally shortest. Each represents 20 births.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How many babies were born during the period 1999–2005?

children.label: d
children.prompt: What percentage of the babies born during the period 1999–2005 were born in 1999?

answer.worked:
140 of the 500 babies were born in 1999.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage born in 1999} &= \left(\frac{140}{500}\times\frac{100}{1}\right)\%\\\text{Percentage born in 1999} &= 28\%\end{align*}$$
